reviews_5s:
These pepper grinders are battery driven by 4 AAA batteries, which provides enough umpf to grind up pepper grains. The main motor appears to have step-down gearing to increase the torque driving the grinder.
The grinder portion itself is a white ceramic surface, which is hard enough to crush/grind dried pepper grains, and coarse salt.
That section also provides for an adjustable opening to select how small you want the pepper powder (or salt) to be.
There is a conveniently positioned button which you press with a thumb, and that activates the grinder, which then emits the pepper particles from the bottom of the grinder. Above the grinding section, is a clear cylindrical receptacle that shows you how much pepper is in it.
Opening it was a little tricky, but not hard to figure out; it screws clockwise about 1/4 turn to open it and you pull it apart, and that opens the receptacle section where you put in the pepper grains. Then push it closed and turn it counter-clockwise to close/resect it, which is a little counter intuitive, but likely due to the direction it turns to grind pepper.
I bought this 3 piece set to grind some specialty peppers. [One type was called grains of paradise, and the other was called whole long pepper.
The grains of paradise were about the proper size for a normal peppercorn (about 2mm diameter) and the grinders handled that fine. However the long pepper was definitely too large for the grinder to reach around to grind, about 1cm in length, so I had to precrush those grains in a mortar/pestle. Once I got them to about 3-4mm, I put them in, and the grinder could handle them quite well.
The pair were both black, and quite nice to look at, and they came with a table base holder that kept them securely upright and together. I have used it for about two months now.
Overall, especially for the price, this was a very nice and practical pepper grinder set.I’ve been using this electric salt and pepper grinder set for a few weeks now, and overall, I’m very pleased with the performance and design.

Pros:

Convenient One-Hand Operation: The one-touch button makes seasoning quick and effortless, especially while cooking or multitasking.

Adjustable Coarseness: Both grinders feature adjustable settings, allowing you to switch between fine and coarse grinds depending on your preference.

Sleek Design: The stainless steel finish looks elegant on the counter or dinner table. It’s modern and matches well with other kitchen appliances.

Refillable and Transparent: The clear container makes it easy to see when it’s time to refill, and the refill process itself is fairly simple.

Cons:

Battery Powered: Each grinder requires several AA batteries, which aren’t included. They’re not rechargeable, which might be a downside for some.

reviews_1s:
I recently purchased an electric salt and pepper shaker, and I have to say, it was a disappointing experience. First off, the design looked promising, but it quickly became clear that it was more style than substance. The mechanism is overly complicated, and I found it frustrating to use. Instead of a simple twist or shake, I had to press a button, which often resulted in uneven dispensing.

The battery life was another letdown. It seemed to run out just when I needed it most, and replacing the batteries was a hassle. Additionally, the grinding quality was inconsistent; sometimes it would produce a fine powder, while other times, it barely dispensed anything at all.

Cleaning was a chore, as the components didn’t come apart easily, and food residue tended to build up inside. I also noticed that the shakers felt flimsy and not particularly durable. Overall, this electric salt and pepper shaker has not lived up to my expectations, and I wouldn't recommend it to anyone looking for a reliable kitchen tool.
